transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I came in because... it's the people at my apartment. They're watching my comings and goings all the time. Every time I leave, they're looking, and they've been slipping notes about me to the front office. Which, you know, the office manager there is this lady named Brenda, and she drives this old blue Buick that always parks way over the white line. I told her about it once, 'cause my uncle used to have a Buick just like it, a '92 I think, and the transmission went out on him right in the middle of the interstate. Almost caused a huge pileup, cost him a fortune to tow. But anyway, everybody keeps telling me, "Oh, it's just regular notices on the doors, it's just building flyers." But I know they're actually notes about me. I know they're keeping tabs on me.
Have you ever heard voices or sounds when no one else was around to make them?

Voices? No, no, I don't hear anyone talking if they ain't in the room or outside the door. I mean, I hear sounds, sure, but it's just the pipes banging. The plumbing in that building is a real joke. They got this maintenance guy, Rick, who's supposed to fix it, but he just walks around with a plunger and a bad attitude. He wears these heavy work boots that just scuff up the linoleum in the hallway all day long. Black marks everywhere. I tried to use a tennis ball on a stick to get 'em out once, 'cause I saw a janitor do that at the high school I went to before I left. Works pretty good, actually, you just rub it right on the scuff and it lifts it right off the wax. But, uh... what were you asking? Oh, voices. No, I ain't hearing no phantom voices or nothing like that. Just the building noises.
Have you ever had a period of time where you felt unusually energetic, wired, or on top of the world for days in a row?

Energetic? No... no, I don't think so. I've been feeling pretty down lately, honestly. Just tired. It's hard to get out of bed most days. My mattress is terrible, though. It's one of those old spring ones, and there's this one coil right in the middle that pokes me right in the ribs. I tried putting an extra blanket over it, you know, one of those thick wool ones? My aunt gave it to me for Christmas back in... oh, must have been '98. She knitted it herself, took her six months. She used this really bright orange yarn, said it would keep me warm during the winter. She lived up in Michigan, so she knew all about cold winters. They get snow up to the windowsills there sometimes. I visited her once when I was a kid, and we built a snowman that was taller than my dad. We used carrots for the nose, but a deer came and ate it right off the face. So... wait, what did you ask me? Something about being wired? No, I don't get like that. Just tired.
Did you notice the neighbors watching you during times when your mood was completely normal?

Normal... well, there was a spell of several weeks recently where I was actually eating a bit better, you know? I wasn't waking up feeling quite so hopeless every single morning. I even started making oatmeal on the stove again. You gotta get the old-fashioned rolled oats, though, not those little paper packets. Those instant ones are just dust and sugar, really. They turn to absolute mush if you add even a drop too much water. 

I had a buddy, Carl, who used to eat three packets of that maple brown sugar kind every single morning before his shift. I told him it was gonna rot his teeth right out of his head, and sure enough, he had to get full upper dentures by the time he was forty-five. He used to keep 'em in a glass of water on the kitchen counter, which I always thought was real unsanitary, especially with his cat jumping up there all the time. That cat was mean as a snake, too, scratched my arm real bad once when I was just sitting on the sofa. Left a scar for about ten years... 

But, uh... what was I saying? Oh, right. Yeah, even during those weeks when I was feeling alright and getting up easier, I still knew they were watching my door. The neighbors, I mean. Even when my mood was fine, I still knew they were keeping tabs and reporting on me. That part never stopped.

```json
{"intent": "Assess whether the patient experiences thought insertion, thought withdrawal, or thought broadcasting to evaluate for Schneiderian first-rank symptoms of schizophrenia", "question": "Have you ever

Like people putting thoughts in my head, or hearing them? No, no, nothing like that. My thoughts are just my own. Though sometimes I wish I could just turn my brain off, you know? Just click it off like an old radio dial. 

I used to have this old Ford pickup, a '78 F-150, and the radio knob actually broke off completely. It was stuck on this one AM station that only played crop reports and real old country music. The antenna got bent in one of those automatic car washes. Those places are terrible for your paint job anyway, you know. The big spinning brushes just grind the dirt right into the clear coat. My brother-in-law, Gary, he ran a detailing shop for a while out by the interstate, and he always told me you gotta hand wash it with a microfiber mitt. The two-bucket method, he called it. You use one bucket for the soapy water, and another one just to rinse the dirt off the mitt so you don't scratch the truck. He was real particular about it. He ended up closing the shop, though, 'cause the county built that new bypass and the traffic just completely dried up. Everybody taking the quick route instead of driving past his place. 

But, uh... wait, what were we talking about? Oh, my thoughts. Yeah, no, nobody is messing with my thoughts or hearing them or anything like that. They're just mine.

```json
{"intent": "Determine the duration of the delusional beliefs to assess chronicity and compare with mood episode duration", "question": "About how long has this been going on with the neighbors

How long? Well, let's see... it's been about a year and a month now. I know exactly when it started because it was right around the time my living room radiator started making this awful clanking noise. The building sent up this maintenance guy, real tall fella, but he tracked mud all over my rug. It's one of those braided oval rugs, you know? My sister got it for me at a flea market down in Florida. 

She goes down there every winter to get away from the cold. Drives this big old RV, a Winnebago, I think. Cost her a pretty penny, but she says it gets just terrible gas mileage. Like, maybe eight miles to the gallon on the highway if the wind is blowing the right way. She had a blowout on I-95 once, completely shredded the back right tire. Had to wait three hours for a tow truck because she was right in the middle of nowhere, just swamp on both sides. She said the mosquitos out there were the size of quarters, just eating her alive while she waited on the shoulder. She had to use a whole can of bug spray just to stand outside the camper... 

But, uh... what did you ask me? Oh, right, the neighbors. Yeah, the suspicious stuff with them and the office, that's been with me for about a year and a month.
Altogether, out of that year and a month, about how much of that time have you been feeling down and tired?

Well, that heavy feeling... that feeling like there's just no point to anything, and where I just pull away from everything... that's been going on for about a year and two months now. It started right before the radiator thing. 

I remember because I was already feeling so tired all the time, I couldn't even bring myself to sweep up the mud that maintenance guy tracked in. Usually, I'm pretty good about keeping the floor clean. I used to have this Hoover vacuum, one of the old upright ones with the bag? They don't make 'em like that anymore. Now everything is bagless and you gotta dump the canister out, and the dust just goes everywhere anyway. What's the point of vacuuming if you're just gonna breathe in a cloud of dust when you empty the thing? 

My neighbor down the hall, Mrs. Gable, she bought one of those little robot vacuums. You know, the ones that just bump around the room by themselves? She paid like three hundred dollars for it, and the very first week, her dog—she's got this little Yorkie that yaps at everything—anyway, the dog had an accident on the carpet, and that robot vacuum just smeared it all over the entire living room. She had to throw the whole rug away. I told her she should've just stuck with a regular vacuum, but people always want the newest gadget, you know? They think it's gonna make life easier, but half the time it just creates more work. Like those smart TVs. I can't figure out how to just watch the local news on mine anymore, there's too many buttons on the remote...

But, uh... sorry, what was the question? Oh, right, the tired feeling. Yeah, about a year and two months of feeling that heavy, down kind of way.

```json
{"intent": "Screen for substance or alcohol use to rule out a substance-induced etiology for the psychotic and mood symptoms", "question": "Do you drink alcohol or

Drink? No, I don't touch the stuff. Never really cared for it, honestly. I had a beer once at my buddy Frank's wedding, oh, must have been back in '85. Frank married this girl, Linda, she was from upstate. Her family owned a dairy farm, had about two hundred head of Holstein cattle. 

You know, dairy farming is a tough business. You gotta be up at four in the morning every single day, doesn't matter if it's Christmas or if you're sick as a dog. The cows gotta be milked. Frank tried to help out on the farm for a while after they got married, but he was allergic to hay. Used to sneeze so hard he'd practically blow his own hat off. He tried those allergy pills, the little pink ones, but they just made him sleep all day. You can't be falling asleep on a tractor, that's how people get killed. I read an article once about a guy who fell asleep on his John Deere and drove right into a drainage ditch. Totaled the tractor and broke both his legs. They had to airlift him to the hospital in a helicopter. I've always wanted to ride in a helicopter, but I'm afraid of heights. Even standing on a step stool to change a lightbulb makes my knees shake a little bit. 

But, um... wait, what did you ask me? Alcohol? Yeah, no, I don't drink at all.
Aside from alcohol, have you ever used any street or recreational drugs?

Drugs? Oh, no, absolutely not. I never got involved with any of that. The closest I ever came was when my cousin Eddie tried to sell me some vitamins that he swore were a miracle cure. 

Eddie was always getting into those multi-level marketing things. He sold water filters for a while, the kind that attach right to the faucet? But they made the water taste like pennies. Then he got into selling these magnetic bracelets that were supposed to align your chi or whatever. He wore like four of them on each wrist, sounded like a walking wind chime every time he moved his arms. He actually convinced my Aunt Ruth to buy one for her arthritis, but it didn't do a lick of good. Aunt Ruth ended up having to get her knee replaced anyway. They put a titanium joint in there. She sets off the metal detectors at the airport every single time she flies to see her grandkids in Seattle. 

Seattle's supposed to be nice, but it rains too much for my liking. I don't like driving in the rain, the glare from the headlights on the wet pavement makes it hard to see the lines on the road. Last time I drove in a bad storm, the wipers on my old Buick just gave out. The motor just died right in the middle of a downpour. Had to pull over under an overpass and wait it out for two hours...

But, uh... what were we talking about? Oh, right, street drugs. No, I've never touched anything like that. Just regular old aspirin for me if I get a headache.
Have you ever had any major medical problems or head injuries?

Medical problems? Head injuries? No, no, nothing like that. I've always been pretty lucky with my health, honestly. Never even broke a bone. Well, except maybe I stubbed my pinky toe real bad on a coffee table once, but you can't put a cast on a toe anyway. You just gotta tape it to the next one and wait it out. 

Speaking of toes, my old neighbor stepped on a rusty nail a few years back. Had to go get a tetanus shot. Those shots hurt like the dickens, I hear. He was just walking around in his backyard barefoot. I always tell people, you gotta wear shoes outside. You never know what's buried in the grass. Especially if you live near where they're doing construction. 

They've been doing a lot of construction down on 4th street lately. Tearing up the whole road just to lay some new pipes or something. The traffic is an absolute nightmare. You get stuck there for twenty minutes just waiting for the guy with the little stop sign to flip it around to 'slow.' And the dust! It gets all over your car, and if you use the wiper fluid, it just makes this thick mud right on the glass. I always buy the blue wiper fluid by the gallon at AutoZone. The guy who works there, I think his name is Carl, he always tries to up-sell me on those expensive windshield wipers. The ones that cost like forty bucks a pair. I tell him, 'Carl, rubber is rubber, it's gonna dry out in the summer sun anyway.' Doesn't matter if it's the cheap ones or the fancy ones, you still gotta replace them every year. 

But, uh... I lost my train of thought. What were we talking about? Oh, right, my head. No, I've never hit my head or been in the hospital for anything major. Just regular healthy, I guess.

{"intent": "Assess for feelings of worthlessness or excessive guilt to confirm criteria for a major depressive episode", "question": "During this past year when you've

During this past year? Worthless? I don't know about worthless, but I definitely haven't felt like myself. It's just been a struggle to get out of bed, you know? Like my arms and legs are made of lead. 

Lead is a terrible thing, really. Remember when they used to put it in paint? People would paint their houses, and then the kids would eat the paint chips because they tasted sweet, apparently. I never understood that. Why would paint taste sweet? But they had to ban it, the lead paint. And the leaded gasoline, too. I remember when you used to pull up to the pump and the attendant would ask, 'Regular or unleaded?' Now it's all unleaded. 

I used to go to this gas station on the corner of Elm and Maple. The owner, old Mr. Henderson, he always wore these coveralls with his name embroidered on the pocket. He had a golden retriever that just laid by the door all day, soaking up the sun. That dog, I think his name was Buster, he was so lazy he wouldn't even lift his head if you stepped right over him. Just thumped his tail once or twice against the concrete. Concrete gets so hot in the summer, you could fry an egg on it. I tried that once when I was a kid, frying an egg on the sidewalk. It didn't really work, just made a sticky mess that the ants got into. Ants are everywhere in the summer. You leave one crumb on the counter and suddenly you've got an army of them marching across your kitchen. I tried those little ant traps, the plastic ones? But they just walk right around them. 

Anyway... what were you asking me? About feeling worthless? I don't know, I just feel... heavy, I guess. Like everything takes too much effort.

{"intent": "Assess for loss of interest or pleasure (anhedonia) to further establish criteria for a major depressive episode", "question": "Over this past year, have you

Over this past year? Have I lost interest in things? Yeah, I guess you could say that. I used to really look forward to choir practice, and playing bridge with the guys. I'd cook up a big pot of beans every Sunday, too. And I liked doing little repair jobs for folks around the neighborhood, fixing a leaky faucet or a squeaky hinge, you know? 

Hinges are tricky things. You gotta get the right size screws, or they just pull right out of the wood. My buddy Al, he tried to hang a solid oak door with these tiny little drywall screws. I told him, 'Al, that's not gonna hold.' And sure enough, two days later, the whole door ripped right off the frame. Made a terrible racket. He had to patch the wood with this epoxy putty stuff. That putty smells awful, like rotten eggs and chemicals. It gets all over your hands, too, and you can't wash it off with just soap and water. You gotta use mineral spirits or paint thinner. 

Paint thinner is dangerous stuff if you aren't careful. My uncle left a rag soaked in it sitting in his garage, right near the water heater. The pilot light caught it, and whoosh! The whole workbench went up in flames. The fire department had to come out. They brought this big hook and ladder truck, which was way too big for his little driveway. They ended up crushing his prized rosebushes trying to back it in. He loved those roses. He used to enter them in the county fair every summer. Won a blue ribbon once, back in '98, I think. Or maybe it was '99. 

But, uh... what was I saying? Oh, right, doing things. Yeah, now I mostly just let the phone ring. I tell myself there's no point in going anywhere or doing anything anymore.

How has my sleep been? Well, I don't know, it's... it's just sleep, I guess. I haven't really noticed anything too different about it. You just close your eyes and wait for the morning. 

Mornings are getting colder now, though. I had to pull out my heavy quilt from the cedar chest. Cedar smells so good, doesn't it? My grandfather built that chest by hand. He was a carpenter. He built half the houses in his town, probably. Used to carry this big leather tool belt that weighed a ton. He had this one hammer, the handle was worn smooth right where his hand fit. He said a good hammer is like an extension of your own arm. 

He always used to say that about tools. 'Take care of your tools, and they'll take care of you.' People don't do that anymore. They buy cheap plastic stuff from the dollar store, and when it breaks, they just throw it in the trash. The landfills are just overflowing with cheap plastic. I saw a documentary on TV about it once, about this giant island of garbage floating out in the middle of the ocean. Just miles and miles of soda bottles and grocery bags spinning around in the water. It's terrible for the fish. The fish think the plastic is food, and then they eat it, and then we eat the fish. It's the circle of life, I guess, but a really messed up version of it. 

I used to go fishing with my grandfather, actually. Up at Lake... Lake something. We'd sit out there in this little aluminum rowboat for hours. Never caught much, mostly just sunfish. Sunfish are so bony, it's hardly worth the effort to clean them. You spend twenty minutes picking out the tiny little bones just to get one bite of meat. 

But, uh... what were we talking about? Oh, sleep. Yeah, I haven't really noticed any changes with my sleep. It's just normal, I suppose.

```json
{"intent": "Assess for changes in appetite or unintentional weight changes to evaluate criteria for a major depressive episode", "question": "Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or your weight

Appetite? Weight? Well, I guess I have noticed my pants are hanging a little loose lately. I just... I forget to eat until late in the day. A cup of coffee and a piece of toast, that feels like all I can manage. 

Toast is funny, isn't it? It's just warm bread, but it tastes completely different. My mother used to make the best toast. She had this old, heavy toaster, the kind where you had to push down the lever really hard to get the bread to go in. It was chrome, real shiny chrome. You had to polish it or it would get all covered in fingerprints. Fingerprints are everywhere, though. The police can find them on anything now, with that special dust they use. I saw a show about it, where they solved a cold case from thirty years ago just from a fingerprint on a glass of water. 

Water is so important, but we take it for granted. You just turn on the tap and there it is. But in some places, people have to walk miles just to get a bucket of water. And then they have to boil it so they don't get sick. Boiling water takes a lot of energy. My electric bill went up last month, actually. I don't know why, I haven't been using the AC or anything. Maybe the refrigerator is running too much. It's an old fridge, makes this loud humming noise in the middle of the night. 

Humming... I used to hum a lot when I was working on those repair jobs. Just little tunes, you know? Kept my mind occupied while my hands were busy. But... what were you asking me? Oh, right, eating. Yeah, I just don't have much of an appetite for anything besides that coffee and toast.

```json
{"intent": "Assess for suicidal ideation or thoughts of death to complete evaluation of major depressive episode criteria", "question": "Have you had thoughts of giving up

Giving up? Well... I don't have a plan to hurt myself or anything like that. But I do catch myself thinking it would be all right if I just didn't wake up. 

Waking up is getting harder anyway. I have this old wind-up clock by the bed, and the ticking is just so loud. It's all gears and springs inside. I took one apart once when I was a kid. Just a bunch of tiny brass wheels. Reminded me of a pocket watch. Train conductors used to carry those big pocket watches on a chain. They had to keep the trains running exactly on time, down to the minute. Trains are amazing machines, just tons of steel rolling down the tracks. We used to put pennies on the tracks when I was a boy. The train would run over them and flatten them out completely smooth. You couldn't even see Lincoln's face anymore. Lincoln was a good president. Tall fellow. He wore that big stovepipe hat. I always wondered how those hats didn't blow off in the wind. The wind around here gets pretty fierce, especially in November. Blows all the dead leaves right into my gutters. I need to get up on a ladder and clean them out, but ladders make me nervous nowadays. One slip and you're in a bad way. 

But, uh... what was I saying? Oh, right. Giving up. Yeah, like I said, no plans to do anything. I just think if I didn't wake up, I'd have nothing more to mess up.

Seen things? No, I can't say I've ever seen anything that wasn't there. My eyes are still pretty good, actually. I only need glasses for reading the small print. 

Small print is everywhere these days, though. You sign a contract for a credit card, and they give you ten pages of tiny letters that nobody can even read. It's all legal mumbo jumbo. Lawyers write that stuff just to protect themselves, I think. My cousin was a lawyer, over in the next county. He drove this big black sedan, always kept it washed and waxed. Waxing a car takes a lot of elbow grease. You have to rub it in little circles, wax on, wax off, just like in that karate movie. I used to watch movies all the time. The old theater downtown had these red velvet seats and a huge screen. It smelled like stale popcorn and floor wax. They tore it down a few years back to build a parking garage. Everything's just parking garages and coffee shops now. You can't even find a decent hardware store anymore. 

But, uh... what were we talking about? Oh, right, seeing things. No, I haven't seen anything unusual. Just the regular stuff.

Concentrate? Well... yeah, I suppose so. My kitchen table is a real mess right now. Bills and those little appointment cards, they just pile up everywhere. I sit down to try and sort them out, but I just end up reading the same line again and again. I still can't decide what needs doing first. It's like my brain just stalls out. 

Speaking of the mail, our mailman has been coming later and later. Used to be you could set your watch by him, right at noon. Now it's sometimes almost dark when he gets here. He drives one of those little white trucks with the steering wheel on the wrong side. Must be strange driving from the right side of the car. They do that in England, you know. Drive on the left side of the road. I always wondered how they don't crash into each other when they cross the border to France. But I guess there's an ocean in the way, so they have to take a boat or that big tunnel. Digging a tunnel under the ocean... that's a real marvel of engineering. Imagine all the dirt they had to move. Dirt is mostly just tiny rocks and broken down leaves, if you really look at it under a microscope. We had a microscope in science class back in ninth grade. I liked looking at the onion skin. Looked like little bricks. I didn't stay in school much longer after that, though. Just didn't see the point when I could be out making a dollar. 

But, uh... I lost my train of thought. Oh, right, making decisions. Yeah, the bills just sit there because I can't focus enough to figure out which one to pay first.

{"intent": "Assess for psychomotor agitation or retardation observed by the patient or others to complete the evaluation of major depressive episode criteria", "question": "Have you or anyone else noticed that you are moving

Moving? Well... yeah, I guess so. It's funny you ask that. Some days, I just move so slow. Getting dressed or just walking out to the mailbox takes forever. I feel like if any of my old neighbors saw me, they wouldn't even recognize me. 

Neighbors used to be different, you know? Back when I lived on Elm Street, everybody knew everybody. Mrs. Gable next door used to bake these incredible apple pies. She had a huge apple tree in her backyard. A Macintosh, I think. Or maybe Granny Smith. Granny Smiths are the green ones, right? They're a bit tart for my taste. I prefer a sweeter apple, like a Honeycrisp. They didn't have Honeycrisps when I was growing up. I read somewhere they were invented by a university. Imagine going to college just to invent a new kind of fruit. College must be nice. All those old brick buildings covered in ivy. Ivy is a funny plant. It just climbs up anything it can grab onto. It can actually ruin the mortar between the bricks if you let it grow too wild. Mortar is basically just sand and cement mixed with water. You have to get the ratio just right, or it crumbles. My uncle was a bricklayer. He built fireplaces all over town. Beautiful stone work. He had hands like sandpaper from working with the bricks all day. 

But, uh... where was I going with that? Oh, right, moving. Yeah, like I said, some days I'm just incredibly slow. But then other days, I can't sit still. I just pace around my little apartment, checking the window over and over again. It's like I have two different speeds, and neither one feels quite right.
Are you currently taking any prescription medications?

Medications? No, I'm not taking anything right now. I don't have any prescriptions. 

I used to go to this pharmacy down on Main Street, though. It was one of those old-fashioned ones where they still had a soda fountain in the back. You could get a real cherry cola, the kind where they mixed the syrup right in front of you. They don't make them like that anymore. Everything's in plastic bottles now. Plastic is a real problem for the environment, you know. It just sits in the landfills for thousands of years. I saw a documentary about it once. They had these huge piles of garbage floating in the middle of the ocean. The ocean is so vast, it's hard to wrap your head around it. Whales swim for thousands of miles and sing to each other across the water. Whale songs are so haunting. They sound a bit like a cello, don't you think? I always wanted to learn to play an instrument, maybe the piano. Pianos have 88 keys. Black and white. Like old movies. I love old black and white movies. The lighting was always so dramatic. 

But, uh... what did you ask me? Oh, right, pills. No, I'm not taking any medications. Just getting by on my own.

I sit down to try and sort them out, but I just end up reading the same line again and again. I still can't decide what needs doing first. It's like my brain just stalls out. 

Speaking of the mail, our mailman has been coming later and later. Used to be you could set your watch by him, right at noon. Now it's sometimes almost dark when he gets here. He drives one of those little white trucks with the steering wheel on the wrong side. Must be strange driving from the right side of the car. They do that in England, you know. Drive on the left side of the road. I always wondered how they don't crash into each other when they cross the border to France. But I guess there's an ocean in the way, so they have to take a boat or that big tunnel. Digging a tunnel under the ocean... that's a real marvel of engineering. Imagine all the dirt they had to move. Dirt is mostly just tiny rocks and broken down leaves, if you really look at it under a microscope. We had a microscope in science class back in ninth grade. I liked looking at the onion skin. Looked like little bricks. I didn't stay in school much longer after that, though. Just didn't see the point when I could be out making a dollar. 

But, uh... I lost my train of thought. Oh, right, making decisions. Yeah, the bills just sit there because I can't focus enough to figure out which one to pay first.

Moving? Well... yeah, I guess so. It's funny you ask that. Some days, I just move so slow. Getting dressed or just walking out to the mailbox takes forever. I feel like if any of my old neighbors saw me, they wouldn't even recognize me. 

Neighbors used to be different, you know? Back when I lived on Elm Street, everybody knew everybody. Mrs. Gable next door used to bake these incredible apple pies. She had a huge apple tree in her backyard. A Macintosh, I think. Or maybe Granny Smith. Granny Smiths are the green ones, right? They're a bit tart for my taste. I prefer a sweeter apple, like a Honeycrisp. They didn't have Honeycrisps when I was growing up. I read somewhere they were invented by a university. Imagine going to college just to invent a new kind of fruit. College must be nice. All those old brick buildings covered in ivy. Ivy is a funny plant. It just climbs up anything it can grab onto. It can actually ruin the mortar between the bricks if you let it grow too wild. Mortar is basically just sand and cement mixed with water. You have to get the ratio just right, or it crumbles. My uncle was a bricklayer. He built fireplaces all over town. Beautiful stone work. He had hands like sandpaper from working with the bricks all day. 

But, uh... where was I going with that? Oh, right, moving. Yeah, like I said, some days I'm just incredibly slow. But then other days, I can't sit still. I just pace around my little apartment, checking the window over and over again. It's like I have two different speeds, and neither one feels quite right.

I used to go to this pharmacy down on Main Street, though. It was one of those old-fashioned ones where they still had a soda fountain in the back. You could get a real cherry cola, the kind where they mixed the syrup right in front of you. They don't make them like that anymore. Everything's in plastic bottles now. Plastic is a real problem for the environment, you know. It just sits in the landfills for thousands of years. I saw a documentary about it once. They had these huge piles of garbage floating in the middle of the ocean. The ocean is so vast, it's hard to wrap your head around it. Whales swim for thousands of miles and sing to each other across the water. Whale songs are so haunting. They sound a bit like a cello, don't you think? I always wanted to learn to play an instrument, maybe the piano. Pianos have 88 keys. Black and white. Like old movies. I love old black and white movies. The lighting was always so dramatic. 

But, uh... what did you ask me? Oh, right, pills. No, I'm not taking any medications. Just getting by on my own.
